name: Brute force: 5+ failed logons in 2 minutes
description: Many failed logons for one user in a short time can mean someone is guessing passwords.

name: New user account created
description: Attackers create accounts to keep access. Check it matches a change ticket.

name: Account added to Administrators group
description: Adding an account to an admin group gives it full control. Always verify.

name: Interactive logon at unusual hour (00:00-05:59)
description: A person logging on at the keyboard in the middle of the night is unusual. Could be stolen credentials, or an admin doing planned work.

name: Connection to known-bad IP
description: Traffic to an IP on the threat-intel list may be malware talking to its controller (C2).

name: DNS lookup of known-bad domain
description: A host asked DNS for a domain on the threat-intel list.

name: EDR: credential dumping behaviour
description: The endpoint agent saw a tool that tries to read stored passwords from memory.

name: Email link clicked to a newly registered domain
description: A user clicked a link in an email that leads to a domain registered in the last 30 days. Phishing sites are usually brand new.

name: Password spraying: one source fails against 5+ different users in 10 minutes
description: One address trying a password or two against many accounts stays under the per-user lockout and the brute-force rule. Count distinct users per source IP instead.

name: Lateral movement: one account logs on over the network to 3+ workstations in 15 minutes
description: People use their own PC. One account hopping across several other workstations over the network is how attackers spread, unless it is planned IT work.

name: Beacon behaviour: regular repeated connections from one host to one IP
description: Malware checks in with its controller on a timer. Six connections to the same IP at near-identical intervals is a beacon pattern, even if the IP is on no intel list.

name: Successful logon from an internet address (203.0.113.x)
description: A successful logon (4624) whose source is an internet address, not a company one, means someone outside got in with a valid account. Failed attempts from the same range are caught by R001 and R009; this rule catches the one that worked.
